title: Trump Announces 50% Tariffs on Canadian Dairy, Alcohol, Vehicles Under Section 338
detail: President Trump announced on July 20, 2026 that his administration will impose additional 50% ad valorem tariffs on a range of Canadian products — dairy, alcoholic beverages, furniture, and motor vehicles — under Section 338 of the Tariff Act, effective 12:01 a.m. ET on August 19, 2026. The move came via three separate proclamations alleging Canadian discrimination against US commerce in those sectors. USTR estimated the tariffs affect nearly $20 billion in annual Canadian imports (reported elsewhere as up to $16 billion for the targeted categories). Analysts described the move as a warning shot to other trading partners ahead of pending Section 301 forced-labor tariff decisions.

media.caption: Trump announces new 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, effective August 19

title: Trump Signs EO 14415 on Defense Supply Chains and Critical Minerals
detail: President Trump signed Executive Order 14415, 'Securing America's Defense Supply Chains and Ensuring Domestic Acquisition of Critical Materials,' on July 20, 2026. The order directs the Department of War to tighten waivers for materials sourced from hostile nations (including China), requires defense contractors to map and screen their supply chains, and delegates Defense Production Act authority to restrict exports of recoverable critical minerals deemed essential to national defense. Agencies must develop a strategy to accelerate qualification of alternative material sources within 90 days (by October 18, 2026).
